newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's Samper hints at public pay flexibility.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's Samper hints at public pay flexibility.

text.p: President Ernesto Samper suggested Thursday that the government may be ready to be flexible on its 13 percent pay offer to public sector workers.
In a press conference in the Caribbean coastal city of Cartagena, where Samper is on holiday, he said the pay deal, due to be fixed Friday, would reflect "austerity and equity".

The government is under pressure to rein back inflation from the 1996 figure of 21.63 percent and to cut public spending in 1997. But the public sectors workers' union FENALTRASE threatened Thursday to launch an imminent strike if the 13 percent salary offer was not raised.

Samper said there may be some margin for introducing weighted salary increases, aimed at reducing pay differentials and giving a bit extra to those sectors whose incomes have been most severely eroded.

Under the terms of a 1995 deal, education workers, who come under the FECODE union, can expect an additional eight percent increase above the 13 percent. The president indicated health workers may also get an additional rise, but mentioned no specific figures.
Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo is scheduled to announce the detailed breakdown of public sector pay rise Friday.
